providers.title: Matrix multiplication with exponent at most 9/4 (OpenAI)
providers.scope: For every eps > 0 there is C_eps such that two n x n complex matrices can be multiplied with at most C_eps n^(9/4+eps) arithmetic operations; thus omega <= 9/4. Proved in the last lesson.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Tensors of bilinear maps
providers.scope: The tensors of a bilinear map in two choices of bases are restrictions of each other; the tensor of a tensor product of bilinear maps is the tensor product of their tensors.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Flattening ranks
providers.scope: Each flattening rank is monotone under restriction, additive on direct sums, multiplicative on tensor products, equal to 1 at the unit tensor and at most the rank.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Matrix multiplication tensors
providers.scope: T_n (x) T_m is isomorphic to T_nm; the three flattening ranks of T_n are n^2, so n^2 <= R(T_n) <= n^3; and T_n restricts to the sum of n unit tensors.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Polynomial multiplication
providers.scope: The tensor C(a,b) of multiplication of polynomials of degrees < a and < b has rank a+b-1 and flattening ranks a, b, a+b-1; exchanging its input legs gives C(b,a).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: From rank to algorithms
providers.scope: If nu <= tau, then for every eps > 0 two n x n complex matrices can be multiplied with O(n^(tau+eps)) arithmetic operations, by recursion on a rank decomposition of some T_u.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Characters on matrix multiplication
providers.scope: Every character satisfies lambda(B_X(m)) = m^(p_X), and similarly for Y and Z, and lambda(T_m) = m^(3t) with t = (p_X+p_Y+p_Z)/3 in [1/3, 1].
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Interpolation
providers.scope: If A' is a degeneration of A (a restriction followed by integer weights and the part of least weight), then lambda(A) >= lambda(A') for every character lambda.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Permuted characters
providers.scope: Composing a character with a permutation of the legs gives a character with the same three exponents in some order; the sum of p_X over the six permutations is 6t.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Finite separation (OpenAI)
providers.scope: If A = A_1 + ... + A_M has a shared X-leg and matched sectors, then 5M copies of A degenerate to the direct sum of the tensors A_h (x) B_X(M), each with its own X-variables.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Counting words
providers.scope: The multinomial coefficient N!/prod (N q_i)! lies between (N+1)^(-s) e^(N H(q)) and e^(N H(q)).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Shared-leg entropy inequality (OpenAI)
providers.scope: For a sum T of nonzero tensors T_i with a shared X-leg and matched sectors, every character lambda and every probability vector q, lambda(T) >= e^(p_X H(q)) prod lambda(T_i)^(q_i).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The symmetrized profile
providers.scope: P(a,b), the 6t-th root of the product of lambda(pi C(a,b)) over the six leg permutations pi, is symmetric, satisfies P(1,b) = b and P(a,b) <= (a+b-1)^(1/t).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Discrete concavity (OpenAI)
providers.scope: 2P(a,b) >= P(a,b+1) + P(a,b-1) for a >= 1 and b >= 2, from a degeneration of C(a,b) (x) B_X(2) built on the exact sequence 0 -> D V_(e-1) -> V_e (x) W -> V_(e+1) -> 0 with D = uw - vs.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Shifted tripling (OpenAI)
providers.scope: P(a, 3h+a-1) >= 3P(a,h) for all a, h >= 1, from a degeneration of C(a, 3h+a-1) into three sectors with a shared X-leg.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Diagonal growth (OpenAI)
providers.scope: A symmetric positive function on pairs of positive integers with P(1,b) = b, discrete concavity and shifted tripling satisfies P(a,a) >= a^(4/3).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The bound on characters (OpenAI)
providers.scope: Every character satisfies t(lambda) <= 3/4, that is, lambda(T_d) <= d^(9/4) for every d.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Compactness of the state space
providers.scope: For the countable field F, the functions 0 <= mu <= R on S form a compact subset of a normed space on which norm and pointwise convergence agree; the detecting states form a compact convex subset.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Finitely generated cones
providers.scope: A finitely generated cone in a finite-dimensional real vector space is closed, and every point outside it is separated from it by a linear functional that is nonnegative on the cone.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Rational solutions
providers.scope: A linear system with rational coefficients that has a nonnegative real solution has a nonnegative rational solution.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Detecting states (OpenAI)
providers.scope: If k < d^nu, there is a state mu with mu(T_d U) >= k mu(U) for all U; otherwise a catalytic comparison E + kU >= E + m + T_d U would force k >= d^nu.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: A multiplicative state
providers.scope: A nonempty compact convex set of states that is mapped into itself by every normalized product mu -> mu(z .)/mu(z) contains a character; the proof uses Schauder's theorem and nested compact sets.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Detecting characters (OpenAI, after Strassen)
providers.scope: For integers d >= 2 and 0 <= k < d^nu there is a character lambda with lambda(T_d) >= k.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The exponent of rank
providers.scope: nu <= 9/4 over the field generated by the roots of unity, and hence over every field containing it.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review
